chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The Banū Umayyah have a fixed period (mirwad) wherein they are having their way. But when differences arise among them then even if the hyena attacks them it will overpower them.

key_terms.الضِّبَاعُ: The hyenas (plural of ضَبْعة, used metaphorically for weaker foes or internal weakness)
key_terms.مِرْوَدًا: A fixed period, limit, or measure of time/dominance
key_terms.يَجْرُونَ فِيهِ: They run/prevail within it (enjoying their way)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'mirwad' and the 'hyena' in the prophecy regarding the Umayyad dynasty?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs the metaphor of a 'merwad' (a designated trough or period of grazing) to illustrate the Umayyads' temporary, divinely permitted tenure of power. He emphasizes that their cohesion is fragile; once internal discord (ikhtilaf) fractures their unity, their structural weakness will be so profound that even a 'dhib' (hyena, symbolizing a minor or weak adversary) would easily conquer them. This reflects the Shia theological principle that political legitimacy is contingent upon unity and justice, and that tyranny inevitably collapses under the weight of its own internal contradictions.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 464. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him,
said: The Banū Umayyah (Umayyids) have a fixed period (mirwad) wherein they are having their way. But when differences arise among them then even if the hyena attacks them it will overpower them.
